newsitem.title: INDIA: I-Sec's expectations of India RBI credit policy.
newsitem.headline: I-Sec's expectations of India RBI credit policy.

text.p: ICICI Securities and Finance Company (I-Sec) said the money market had high expectations in the credit policy to be announced by the Reserve Bank of India later this month.

"Expectations from the forthcoming busy season credit policy ride high with the market already having discounted a CRR (cash reserve ratio) cut though at the cost of a corresponding lowering of the export refinance limits," it said in its latest debt market update.
It said the objective of the credit policy would be to give a boost to the sagging credit demand and to signal lower interest rates to the market.

"However, implementation of a CRR cut will have to be weighted against its inflationary impact through monetary expansion, particularly since the current rate of inflation at 6.25 percent is two percent higher than the end-March figure."
It said the recent hike in petroleum product prices has largely been reflected in the wholesale price index.

I-Sec said another possible measure to encourage banks to further reduce their prime lending rates would be to lower the maximum deposit rate offered by banks on deposits less than one year from the current 11 percent cap.
"The Reserve Bank is also likely to issue guidelines for the proposed satellite dealer network as a sequel to the setting up of primary dealers in government securities," it said.
A boost to the commercial paper market could be given by the reintroduction of the facility of stand-by guarantee, it said.
